The refactor compiles and behavior is **byte-for-byte identical** to baseline — same JSON response (`customerCode":"TOW-SUR-0001"`, `locality":"NSW"`, `membershipNumber":"TOW-SUR-0001-M26"`, `checkDigit":8`) and the same audit line. ## What I changed (preparation only, no behavior change)

The change touches three focal points; I reshaped each so the real edit lands as a small, local swap rather than as new complexity piled into these methods.

**1. `OwnerRestControllerV1` — shared SHA-256 hex helper**
`householdIdFor` had the SHA-256 digest loop (get instance → hash UTF-8 → format `%02X` → try/catch) inlined. The upcoming `HASH8` would have duplicated that verbatim. I extracted it into one `shaHex(input, hexChars)` helper — the codebase's "single definition" idiom — and routed `householdIdFor` through it (`shaHex(key, 16)`, identical output). The new customer-code hash becomes `shaHex(telephone + lastName, 8)` with no new plumbing.

**2. `OwnerRestControllerV1.nextCustomerCode` — takes the `Owner`**
Was `nextCustomerCode(city, lastName)`. The new identity needs postcode + telephone + lastName, and (unlike today) no owner-list lookup. I changed the signature to `nextCustomerCode(Owner owner)`, reading `city`/`lastName` off it internally — same computation today, but the method now already has every field the new formula needs. This also keeps the **`addOwner`** call site (`nextCustomerCode(owner)`) stable, so that focal point needs no touch when the change lands.

**3. `OwnerMapper.locality` — isolated region source**
`locality` computed region inline (`owner.getRegion()`) and rendered `null → "UNKNOWN"`. I split the region source into `localityRegion(owner)` (currently returns `owner.getRegion()`), leaving `locality` owning only the `UNKNOWN` rendering. The change ("derive locality from the region-and-hash identity") becomes a one-method body swap without disturbing the fallback, and without pushing customer-code-format parsing into the mapper.

`membershipNumber`, `checkDigit`, and the audit line already read `customerCode` opaquely, so they follow the new identity automatically — no prep needed and none added. No dead code was introduced: every new helper is used on the current path.
